concept.title: Best Practices
concept.shortdesc: Follow recommended maintenance and security practices to keep the home network secure, stable, and available.

conbody.p: Regular network maintenance can prevent security problems, configuration loss, and unexpected connection problems.
Keep the up to date, protect network credentials, back up the router configuration, and review connected devices regularly.
conbody.note: Perform each maintenance activity regularly. Keep a record of important network changes.
Define a maintenance schedule for firmware reviews, configuration backups, credential reviews, and connected-device audits.

section.title: Regular Firmware Updates
section.p: Firmware controls the operation of the . Firmware updates can correct software problems, improve device compatibility, and provide security corrections.
Check for approved firmware updates regularly. Use the update function in the or get approved firmware from the .
section.note: Back up the router configuration before you install a firmware update.
Install only firmware intended for and the applicable .
Do not turn off the router or disconnect its power supply during a firmware update.
Review the firmware release information before installation. Test network connectivity, wireless security, guest access, IoT connectivity, and custom settings after the update.
section.p: For more information, see .

section.title: Periodic Password Review
section.p: Review the passwords for the primary Wi-Fi network, guest network, administrator account, and connected devices.
Each password must be long, unique, and difficult to guess. Use different passwords for the Wi-Fi network and the .
Change a password when:

ul.li: The password is a default password.
An unauthorized person knows or can access the password.
An unknown device connects to the network.
The password is stored in an unprotected location.
An authorized user no longer requires network access.
An applicable security policy requires a password change.

section.note: A password change disconnects devices that use the previous password. Update all authorized devices with the new password.
Store network passwords in a trusted password manager or another secure location.

Do not change passwords only because a fixed period has passed unless an applicable policy requires the change. Change a password immediately when exposure, unauthorized access, or another security problem is suspected.
section.p: For more information, see .

section.title: Configuration Backups
section.p: A configuration backup contains the saved settings for the . A backup can help restore the network after a configuration error, hardware replacement, or factory reset.
Create a backup after the initial configuration and after an important network change.
Important network changes can include:

ul.li: A changed Wi-Fi network configuration
A changed guest network configuration
A changed DHCP configuration
A new access point or mesh node
A changed access-control rule
A firmware update
A changed administrator configuration

section.note: Store the backup file in a secure location. The file can contain network settings and other sensitive information.
Do not edit the backup file manually. An invalid backup file can cause configuration errors.

Record the product model, hardware version, firmware version, backup date, and applicable configuration changes with each backup. Confirm compatibility before you restore a backup to different hardware or firmware.
section.p: For more information, see .

section.title: Connected-Device Monitoring
section.p: Review the devices connected to the home network regularly. This review helps identify unknown or unauthorized devices.
Sign in to the and open the . Compare the connected-device list with the devices that you recognize.
Review devices connected to:

ul.li: The primary network identified by
The guest network identified by
Available wired LAN ports
The or

section.p: A connected device can appear by its device name, hostname, IP address, or MAC address.
section.note: Verify the device name and MAC address before you block or remove a device. Some client devices use private or randomized MAC addresses.
If you do not recognize a device, compare the displayed information with the network settings on your computers, smartphones, printers, televisions, and smart home devices.

Review connection times, assigned IP addresses, access points, traffic use, and network membership when this information is available. Investigate unusual changes in device identity or connection behavior.

section.title: Recommended Maintenance Schedule

strow.stentry: Regularly and when an unknown connection is suspected
Regularly and after a security notice
Regularly and after suspected password exposure
After initial setup and after an important configuration change
After a security or guest-network configuration change
Regularly and when a device no longer receives security updates
After firmware, hardware, or configuration changes

section.note: The maintenance frequency depends on the network environment, security requirements, and number of connected devices.

section.title: Maintenance Records
section.p: Keep a record of important network maintenance activities.
Record the following information:

ul.li: The date and time of the maintenance activity
The name of the changed device
The reason for the change
The configuration settings that changed
The firmware version before and after an update
The configuration backup file name
The connectivity tests that were completed
The result of each test

section.note: Do not record Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, access tokens, or other confidential credentials in the maintenance record.
Use a controlled change record when several administrators manage the network. Include a rollback method for an important configuration change.

section.title: Secure Network Configuration
section.p: Maintain the following security settings:

ul.li: Use when all required devices support it.
Use a unique password for the primary Wi-Fi network.
Use a different password for the .
Keep remote management disabled when it is not required.
Use for visitor devices.
Isolate IoT devices when the router supports network isolation.
Remove devices that are no longer authorized.

section.note: Review access-control, DHCP reservation, port-forwarding, DNS, remote-management, and network-isolation settings. Remove rules that are no longer required.

section.title: Verify Network Operation
section.p: Test the network after a firmware, credential, hardware, or configuration change.
Verify the following conditions:

ul.li: Authorized wired and wireless devices can connect.
Client devices can access Internet services.
The primary network uses the required security mode.
The guest network provides Internet access but cannot access the primary network.
IoT devices can use only the network services that they require.
The is available only to authorized administrators.

section.note: Record the verification results. Restore the approved configuration or reverse the change if the network does not operate correctly.
